name: Pelet
title: Warrior in David's army
summary: Pelet is a name that appears several times in the Old Testament. The most well-known Pelet was the son of Jahdai from Caleb's lineage in the tribe of Judah. Another Pelet, the son of Asmaveth, was among the brave warriors who joined David in Ziklag while he fled from King Saul.

keyEvents.title: Pelet in Caleb's genealogy
keyEvents.description: Pelet is mentioned as the son of Jahdai in the genealogy of Caleb in the tribe of Judah, placing him within an important lineage in Israel.

keyEvents.title: Pelet joins David in Ziklag
keyEvents.description: Pelet, the son of Asmaveth, was among the Benjaminite warriors who left Saul to join David while he was staying in Ziklag.

keyEvents.title: David's mighty men gather
keyEvents.description: The brave men who came to David were skilled warriors capable of using both their right and left hands with sling and bow, and Pelet was among them.

keyEvents.title: The loyalty of the Benjaminites to David
keyEvents.description: Even though Saul was from the tribe of Benjamin, several Benjaminites, including Pelet, chose to leave Saul and support David as God's chosen king.
